chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Suleyman Al-Ja'fary who said:

I heard Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying regarding the Statement of Allah, Blessed and High: 'When they spend the night in what displeases Him in speech,' he said: 'It means So-and-so and So-and-so, and Abu Ubaydah ibn Al-Jarrah.'

key_terms.أَبُو عُبَيْدَةَ بْنَ الْجَرَّاحِ: Abu Ubaydah ibn Al-Jarrah (a companion of the Prophet)

ai.seo_question: Who does the Imam identify as the subjects of the verse 'Ith yubayyituna' in Surah An-Nisa?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) provides a specific exegetical application of Surah An-Nisa, verse 108, identifying the 'prominent companions' (Fuqaaha) who spent the night in speech displeasing to Allah as Abu Bakr, Umar, and Abu Ubaydah ibn Al-Jarrah. This interpretation highlights the Shia scholarly view that these key figures engaged in significant nocturnal deliberations or disputes, the content of which was not fully pleasing to divine will, thereby linking Quranic revelation directly to early Islamic political and scholarly history.

en.hubeali: H 14973 – Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al-Husayn Bin Saeed, from Suleyman Al-Ja’fary who said:

I heard Abu Al-Hassanasws saying regarding the Statement of Allahazwj Blessed and High: “[4:108] They seek to hide from men and seek not to hide from Allah. He is with them when by night they hold discourse displeasing unto Him”, heasws said: ‘It means so and so and so and so (Abu Bakr and Umar), and Abu Ubeyda Bin Al-Jarrah’.
en.sarwar: 526. Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, and someone else, from Mansour Bin Yunus, from Ibn Azina, from Abdullah Bin Najjashy who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (a.s.) saying regarding the Statement of Allah (azwj) Mighty and Majestic: “[4:63] These are they of whom Allah knows what is in their hearts; therefore turn aside from them and admonish them, and speak to them effectual words concerning themselves”, Meaning, by Allah (azwj), so and so and so and so (Abu Bakr and Umar). “[4:64] And We did not send any messenger but that he should be obeyed by Allah’s permission; and had they, when they were unjust to themselves, come to you and asked forgiveness of Allah and the Messenger had (also) asked forgiveness for them, they would have found Allah Oft-returning (to mercy), Merciful”, Meaning, by Allah (azwj), the Prophet (saww) and Ali (a.s.) due to what they had done to him (a.s.). Yes, had they come to you (a.s.) with it, O Ali (a.s.), and asked forgiveness of Allah and the Messenger had (also) asked forgiveness for them, they would have found Allah Oft-returning (to mercy), Merciful. “[4:65] But no! by your Lord! they do not believe (in reality) until they make you a judge of that which has become a matter of disagreement among them”. So Abu Abdullah (a.s.) said: ‘By Allah (azwj), it is Ali (a.s.) who is Meant by it. and then do not find any straightness in their hearts as to what you have decided, upon your (saww) tongue, O Rasool Allah (saww), Meaning by it the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) and submit with entire submission to Ali (a.s.)’.
